name: ancestor altar
description: A bàn thờ: a tall lacquered altar table with framed photographs of the family's dead, a brass incense bowl, fruit offerings and flickering electric candles.  Every home and shop in the city keeps one, high up and facing the door.

name: concrete power pole
description: A tapered concrete pole carrying the neighbourhood's electricity, phone and cable TV lines, plus decades of abandoned ones.  The cables sag between the houses in black loops and knot into a nest halfway up that no linesman has dared to untangle.

name: ward loudspeaker
description: A steel pole topped with a pair of horn loudspeakers, the loa phường.  Every morning at six it read out ward notices, health campaigns and the price of rice.  Since the fever it repeated the same quarantine message, and now it is silent.

name: stainless street table
description: A low, square stainless-steel table of the kind every sidewalk eatery stacks at closing time, with a caddy of chopsticks, chili sauce and fish sauce still on it.

name: bánh mì cart
description: A street vendor's cart: a glass case on a wheeled blue cabinet, with a gas burner for warming the bread and jars of pickles and pâté.  The baguettes inside are going stale.

name: sidewalk umbrella
description: A big striped umbrella on a weighted stand, shading a café's stools from the afternoon sun.

name: sidewalk sign
description: A painted A-frame sign set out on the sidewalk to point customers into a shop: phở, motorbike repair, photocopies, phone cards.
